copyright: Marie Lake, John Muir Wilderness near Bishop, California, United States (© Steve Dunleavy/Getty Images)
description: If mountains could keep a record of the past, the John Muir Wilderness near Bishop, California, United States, would have plenty to share. Its valleys, lakes and granite formations reveal a history shaped over millions of years. Established in 1964, this vast protected area spans more than 2,600 square kilometres of the Sierra Nevada and is named after naturalist John Muir. Today, parts of the Pacific Crest Trail and John Muir Trail pass through the area, drawing hikers into one of the largest high-elevation wilderness regions in the contiguous United States.

copyright: Lemon shark pup in mangrove forest, Eleuthera, Bahamas (© Shane Gross/Nature Picture Library)
description: On 14 July, Shark Awareness Day asks us to trade movie panic for ocean truth. Sharks have patrolled the seas for more than 420 million years, and as apex predators, they help keep marine ecosystems in balance.

copyright: Antelope Canyon on the Navajo Nation, east of Page, Arizona, United States (© Mark Skalny/Getty Images)
description: International Rock Day, observed on 13 July, celebrates the geological building blocks beneath our feet and encourages curiosity about how rocks shape Earth's landscapes and history. From ancient tools to modern mineral uses, rocks hold clues to volcanic eruptions, shifting continents and the evolution of life over millions of years. In India, the vast Deccan Traps stand as a dramatic reminder of the powerful volcanic forces that have shaped our planet.

copyright: Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument, Maine, United States (© Cavan Images/Offset/Shutterstock)
copyrightKeyword: Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument
description: If you're looking for Maine in the United States at its most untamed, this is it. Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument spans more than 350 square kilometres of rugged North Woods wilderness, where still ponds reflect the sky and dense forests seem to absorb every sound.

copyright: Port de Saint-Goustan, Auray, Brittany, France (© Rolf E. Staerk/Shutterstock)
description: In France, Port de Saint-Goustan lies just below Auray's upper town, where a narrow tidal inlet along the Auray River opens towards the Gulf of Morbihan. The harbour sits along the Auray River, also known locally as the Loc’h, creating its sheltered, storybook setting. In the 13th century, the Dukes of Brittany built a bridge, a port and a castle here; the fortress has long since disappeared, but cobbled quays, winding lanes and timber-framed houses still line the waterfront.

copyright: Aerial view of land and ocean, Victoria, Australia (© Nearmap/Getty Images)
description: Land or sea? In Victoria, you don't have to choose. This southeastern Australian state proves that the best adventures come with a little of both.

copyright: Rice fields at Sapa, Lào Cai, Vietnam (© Anujak Jaimook/Getty Images)
description: Sunlight breaks through drifting clouds and settles on the terraced slopes of Sapa, where rice fields spill down the mountainsides in sweeping layers like a living staircase. Nestled in Vietnam's Lào Cai Province, this highland region is shaped as much by human endeavour as by nature. For centuries, farmers from ethnic communities such as the Hmong have carved and maintained these terraces, channelling water across steep hillsides to nourish each growing season.
